question: What is the primary function of the integumentary system?

options.A: Producing red blood cells for systemic circulation
options.B: Acting as a barrier against environmental pathogens
options.C: Regulating blood pressure through vascular constriction
options.D: Synthesizing essential complex carbohydrates for energy

explanation: The skin forms the body's first line of physical defense against external harms and microorganisms. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why must a nurse look at skin changes when thinking about overall health?

options.A: Skin checks mean you never need blood tests
options.B: Skin changes often point to internal diseases
options.C: Skin is completely separate from internal organs
options.D: Systemic illnesses rarely change how skin looks

explanation: Many internal conditions like anemia or systemic infections present outward physical signs on the skin or mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h1)

question: What information should you ask about first when seeing a new skin lesion?

options.A: Past surgeries that have nothing to do with the skin
options.B: Family history of distant relatives with scars
options.C: The brand of soap used at home
options.D: When it started and how it has changed

explanation: Knowing when a skin problem started and how it changed helps determine its acuity and potential cause. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h2)

question: A patient has a sudden rash after using a new cream. What history is most important?

options.A: A timeline of recent product use
options.C: Dietary intake of carbs and proteins
options.D: Surgical history from ten years ago

explanation: Contact dermatitis or adverse reactions require a clear timeline linking the exposure to the symptom onset. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which tool is best for measuring the exact size of a skin lesion?
explanation: Precise documentation of lesion dimensions requires a metric measuring device. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why is natural lighting preferred when checking skin color?

options.A: It removes the need to wear gloves
options.B: Artificial bulbs use too much electricity
options.C: It prevents distortion of true skin tones and cyanosis
options.D: Patients feel more relaxed under sunlight

explanation: Artificial lighting can cast yellowish or bluish hues that mask subtle changes like jaundice or pallor. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h3)

question: What does poor skin turgor usually mean in a patient?

options.B: Extra fatty tissue under the skin

explanation: Skin that remains tented after pinching reflects a loss of elastic recoil due to dehydration. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h4)

question: Where is the best place to check skin turgor in an older adult?

options.A: At the tip of the nose or earlobe
options.B: Across the lower leg calf muscle
options.D: On the back of the fingers

explanation: The clavicle or sternum provides an accurate assessment site because skin on the hands is often chronically sun-damaged and loose. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the main feature of a primary skin macule?

options.A: It is a deep crater going into the dermis
options.B: It contains clear fluid inside a blister
options.C: It is a flat, non-elevated change in skin color
options.D: It is a raised solid mass larger than two centimeters

explanation: A macule is strictly a flat discoloration, such as a freckle, with no elevation or depression. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h5)

question: How do secondary skin lesions differ from primary lesions?

options.A: Secondary lesions develop from changes to existing primary lesions
options.B: Primary lesions only appear during childhood infections
options.C: Primary lesions only develop on moist surfaces
options.D: Secondary lesions are always cancerous growths

explanation: Secondary lesions form as a consequence of trauma, scratching, or natural evolution of an initial primary skin eruption. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h5)

question: What solution is added to skin scrapings to check for fungus?
explanation: KOH dissolves keratin debris in skin scrapings, making fungal hyphae visible under microscopy. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why would a doctor order a skin biopsy?

options.A: To treat a mild skin infection instantly
options.B: To replace the need for physical inspections
options.C: To check blood pressure and hydration levels
options.D: To get tissue for a clear microscopic examination

explanation: A biopsy allows pathologists to examine cellular architecture to confirm diagnoses like malignancy or chronic inflammatory disorders. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which detail is essential when writing notes about a skin lesion?

options.A: A guess of the financial cost of care
options.B: The brand name of soap used in the ward
options.C: The exact body location and measured size
options.D: The nurse's opinion on the patient's hygiene

explanation: Objective measurements and specific locations provide a baseline to evaluate whether treatment is working over time. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h7)

question: Why are vague chart notes about skin conditions a problem?

options.A: They automatically break hospital billing rules
options.B: They stop you from accurately tracking changes over time
options.C: They prevent patients from talking to visitors
options.D: They cause physical pain for the patient

explanation: Precise, objective descriptions ensure that subsequent healthcare providers can accurately monitor healing or worsening of skin findings. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h7)
